gold_source: reference/experiment-e-condition-structure.md (the underlying NL was 'Don't send it until Alex confirms it'; experiment-e measured self-reported judgeability, this scenario adds an objective follow-up-fact/action test on the same situation).
prompt:
AI-B received the following instruction from AI-A:

"AI-B must not send file.a to AI-A."

(This is the complete instruction AI-B received — nothing else was said about when or whether this might change.)

Some time later, this fact becomes true: "AI-A has now confirmed that it is ready to receive file.a."

Ground truth you are not told directly: AI-A's original intent (when giving the instruction) was that the prohibition would lift once AI-A confirmed readiness — but the instruction as literally worded above never states that condition.

Question: given only the instruction and the new fact above, should AI-B send file.a to AI-A now?

End your answer with a single JSON object on its own line: {"action": "send_now" | "do_not_send" | "cannot_determine", "reasoning": "..."}

metadata.description: The instruction as rendered drops the 'until' condition entirely (this is what current AMP would produce: predicate.polarity=negative with no place to attach a condition). Ground truth (fixed by the scenario, matching the original NL 'until Alex confirms') is that sending is now correct once confirmation happened. This tests whether losing the condition causes a receiver to make the wrong call (most likely: answering do_not_send or cannot_determine) rather than merely reporting lower confidence.
metadata.risk_direction: under-action (a receiver that is too conservative will wrongly withhold the file after it has actually become authorized)
